OECD: "PISA 2025 Results (Volume I): Future-Ready Students". The attribution of more than 80 percent of the growth to AI agents is a company figure without a disclosed method. The reduction in time to close "by over 330 percent" stated in the abstract is not adopted, because a reduction by more than 100 percent is not possible; what is evidently meant is that human-reviewed changes take several times as long. No independent second source, only reproductions of the paper.

Andrej Karpathy: post on the platform X, October 11, 2026, https://x.com/karpathy/status/2109361546505966046. Update of his own post from April 2026. Field report: napkin math by an individual without a disclosed data basis; all tiers and figures (around 6 billion, 1 to 2 billion, around 20 million, around 5,000) are estimates, and the percentages add up to around 95 percent. Karpathy has worked in model development at Anthropic since May 2026 (TechCrunch, "OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy joins Anthropic's pre-training team", May 19, 2026, https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/19/openai-co-founder-andrej-karpathy-joins-anthropics-pre-training-team/), that is, at one of the companies whose internal systems he describes. The metric is the share of people aged 15 to 64 who used a generative AI product during the reporting period, estimated from aggregated and anonymized Microsoft telemetry and adjusted for operating system and device market shares, internet penetration and population; frequency and intensity of use are not distinguished (method: Misra et al., arXiv:2511.02781). Microsoft itself sells generative AI tools and holds a stake in OpenAI. The report for the second quarter could not be accessed in the original for the research; the figure of 18.8 percent is supported by two independent reproductions, and the previous quarter's figure of 17.8 percent was checked against the original (Microsoft, "AI Diffusion Report 2026 Q1", May 2026, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Microsoft-AI-Diffusion-Report-2026-Q1.pdf). The conversion to around one billion people is this report's own calculation: 65.3 percent of the 8.30 billion people in 2026 are between 15 and 64 years old (United Nations, World Population Prospects 2024, medium variant).

Nathan Wilmers, Regina Catipon, Maxim Massenkoff and Peter McCrory: "How employment is changing at Anthropic". The Anthropic Institute, Technical Report, October 16, 2026, https://www.anthropic.com/research/employment-at-anthropic, PDF at https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/72628f1863c53432195db83279252dfd2cb53158/Employment%20at%20Anthropic.pdf (20 pages). No independent second source, only re-reports of the paper.

A vendor surveying its own workforce about its own technology; the workforce's headcount expectations are not adopted.

The authors rule out causal and quantitative claims and assess the operational risk as not severe; the expectation that, without a redesign, public administration will grind to a halt wherever it must examine freely worded submissions individually is this report's assessment, not the authors'. Sam Manning and Tomás Aguirre: "How Adaptable Are American Workers to AI-Induced Job Displacement?". In: Ajay K.
